title: How many things really describe an incident
question: How many independent dimensions are hidden in the dozens of yes/no flags that describe each incident?

prep_steps: Used 37 0/1 incident flags with non-zero variance
Standardised each flag to mean 0, SD 1 before PCA

why: The 37 flags overlap heavily (a ransomware flag implies a malware flag, an error flag often comes with media assets), so PCA can compress them into a few uncorrelated components. Kaiser's rule keeps 12 components and 80% of the variance needs 14, which measures how much redundancy there is.

data_properties.name: Components for 80% variance
data_properties.implication: Dimensions needed to keep most information.

alternatives.why_not: Flags are binary and FA assumes continuous, roughly normal indicators; it is used on NCRB rates instead.
PC1 and PC2 alone carry 29% of the variance, so plots and clustering on raw flags would be noisy.

yields: The 37 incident flags boil down to about 12 independent patterns by Kaiser's rule (14 to keep 80% of the information), led by +action_hacking / +actor_external. That is 32% as many dimensions as flags, so the flags overlap but each still adds information; CyCRS keeps the separate attack categories rather than replacing them with components.
limitations: PCA on binary flags is descriptive; components are linear summaries, not causal factors.
Rare flags get large standardised values and can dominate later components.
